description: Hi! I'm Vaidehi, a CE final-year from Pune. We're tackling "Flame in Freefall" to turn decades of NASA microgravity fire research into a source-cited AI tool for Moon & Mars missions. Looking for:- Data/ML: Python, PDF parsing, data extraction; Frontend: React. If you want to build a high-quality project that NASA judges will take seriously, join us!
summary: We read NASA’s raw flight videos and found where the evidence stops. Fireline Atlas connects measurements from 65 space-station fire tests to NASA’s BASS-II experiment records. In 24 clips, the visible flame signal faded close in time to a drop in the radiometer reading. Five still showed a visible signal near the end, and 36 remained inconclusive. Researchers can select a test to inspect the evidence behind its classification. The results map reveals a second gap: across all 129 NASA records, the highest initial oxygen concentration was 22.2%. The challenge’s Moon base scenario starts at 30%. Fireline makes that gap visible so researchers can see where new experiments are needed.
details:
Fireline Atlas helps researchers answer a practical question: What can a flame aboard the International Space Station tell us about fire in a Moon base? We built an interactive dashboard that connects 129 NASA BASS-II experiment records with measurements from 65 flight videos. A researcher can select a test, inspect what the camera saw, compare it with an instrument reading, and trace the result back to the NASA source.

In test B1, for example, the visible flame signal fades near 38 seconds. At 39.75 seconds, the radiometer reading falls below our comparison level. Fireline shows both observations so researchers can judge the evidence themselves. Across all 65 clips, 24 showed a loss of visible signal close to a radiometer drop, five still had a visible signal near the end of observation, and 36 remained inconclusive. Dim flames, work lights, and missing sensor readings can make the outcome uncertain.

The results map plots initial oxygen against recorded duct airflow for the 25 tests with a single numeric value for both. Each dot opens its experiment record. The highest initial oxygen concentration in all 129 records was 22.2%, while the challenge’s lunar habitat scenario starts at 30%. That gap identifies a question for future experiments. In Flame Lab, users can also track a moving boundary across 11 timestamped NASA images and see how changing the brightness threshold affects the measurement. Mission Review helps users compare test conditions with a proposed habitat and export a follow-up experiment plan.

How we used SI. We used OpenAI Codex and Anthropic’s Claude to brainstorm approaches, research NASA sources, write and debug code, develop the flight-video measurement scripts, review results, and prepare the submission text and demo. Our team chose the flight-video approach and made the final project decisions. The demo uses a Fish Audio–generated voice. NASA supplied the original experiment records, images, and footage. Fireline’s Python analysis produced the derived measurements, and the browser dashboard displays them alongside their sources and limitations.
